headline: Hitler purged his own party in June and became head of state in August, and Hollywood started enforcing its code
texture: The Nazis turned on the Sturmabteilung between June 30 and July 2 and killed its leadership along with other inconvenient people. Hindenburg died a month later and Hitler combined the presidency with the chancellorship on August 2, which left nothing above him. The sixth Nuremberg rally ran in September. In China, the Communists set out on the Long March on October 16 and were still walking at the end of the year.

The Hays Code began to be enforced strictly on July 1, four years after the studios had written it, and what a film could show narrowed overnight. Kid Millions led the box office and It Happened One Night came fourth, then took Best Picture, Best Director, Best Actor and Best Actress, which nothing had done before.

Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow were shot dead by police in Bienville Parish on May 23. John Dillinger had robbed a bank in Mason City in March. Italian and Ethiopian troops exchanged fire in December after a boundary commission found an Italian fort where it should not have been, which is how the next war started.

notes: Research pass July 2026. No prices section: the three price series all start later. It Happened One Night taking the top five awards is stated as five categories, which is the standard account, though the source line names only the film. The remark that the Ogaden fort is how the next war started is a judgement, not a sourced claim, and comes out if challenged.
